entry.title: Flide: Accelerating Decision Inference with Exact State Forking
entry.summary:
Decision models such as Jev have emerged as a highly promising paradigm for LLM agent systems, providing lightweight and reliable categorical reasoning for rapid System One execution. However, existing generation-oriented inference engines fail to support these workloads effectively, suffering from severe prefix recomputation overheads or distorted output probabilities. To address this challenge, we propose Flide, an efficient and exact inference engine that decouples the logical tree structure of a decision request from its physical execution within a single flattened token stream.

Source: Hugging Face Daily Papers · Tags: #llm #open-weights #combinatorics #inference

entry.title: Doom GPU Flame Graphs
entry.summary:
Imagine halving the resource costs of AI and what that could mean for the planet and the industry -- based on extreme estimates such savings could reduce the total US power usage by over 10% by 2030 1 . At Intel we've been creating a new analyzer tool to help reduce AI costs called AI Flame Graphs : a visualization that shows an AI accelerator or GPU hardware profile along with the full software stack, based on my CPU flame graphs . Our first version is available to customers in the Intel Tiber AI Cloud as a preview for the Intel Data Center GPU Max Series (previously called Ponte Vecchio).

Source: Brendan Gregg (Systems Performance & eBPF) · Tags: #kernel-os #performance #compilers #combinatorics

entry.title: KORD: Breaking the Key-Generation Bottleneck in Dealerless Function Secret Sharing via Protocol–Hardware Co-Design
entry.summary:
Function secret sharing (FSS) has emerged as a promising technique for secure multi-party computation (MPC), offering a lightweight online phase. However, existing FSS-based private inference frameworks typically rely on trusted dealers to generate and distribute large amounts of offline key material (e.g., 16.8 GiB for BERT-base), incurring substantial overhead in key generation, transfer, storage, and parsing. Cryptographic dealer-free FSS eliminates the trusted dealer but introduces costly interaction during key generation.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #rust #combinatorics

entry.title: Independent Leakage Does Not Save Evasive LWE: Refuting Folklore Fixes in the Private-Coin Setting
entry.summary:
The evasive learning with errors (evasive LWE) assumption has enabled a wide range of advanced cryptographic constructions from lattices in the past few years. The simple intuition that LWE remains secure even when additional ``non-zeroizing'' short preimages are given has proved highly versatile in applications. Unfortunately, recent counterexamples have refuted its general private-coin formulations, showing that having the short preimages along with arbitrary auxiliary leakage about the secret and target matrices can invalidate this intuition.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #post-quantum #combinatorics
